extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: SWE-Gym is an environment for training software engineering (SWE) agents and verifiers. It contains 2,438 real-world task instances from 11 popular open-source Python repositories, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Repositories were filtered using SEART GitHub search for Python repositories created before July 1, 2022 with more than 500 stars, at least 300 lines of code, more than 500 pull requests, and 100 contributors (yielding 358 repositories). Using SWE-Bench's instance extraction script, 64,689 task instances were extracted as SWE-Gym Raw. For 11 repositories, environments were versioned and dependencies were manually configured and verified.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real-world pull requests and GitHub issues from open-source Python repositories on GitHub.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Dependencies were manually configured using configuration files (e.g., requirements.txt), CI scripts, or repository documentation at the time of issue creation. SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script was run to ensure gold patches passed more unit tests than the original code, and instances that failed validation were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual configuration of dependencies for each task instance using relevant configuration files, CI scripts, or documentation from the repository snapshot at the time of issue creation, followed by execution-based validation ensuring gold patches pass unit tests.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Automating software engineering could increase developer productivity and accessibility across industries, and support open-source infrastructure. However, capable agents may impact software engineering employment, raise questions regarding code ownership, licensing, and attribution, and carry potential risks of misuse for automated creation of malicious code.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The task distribution across repositories follows a long-tail distribution (e.g., pandas accounts for nearly one-third of instances, whereas bokeh accounts for 1%). Additionally, repeated sampling shows task success probabilities follow a long-tail pattern biased toward easier tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limited environment diversity, including the number of repositories (11 repositories), types of tasks, and programming languages (restricted to Python).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating language model-based software engineering agents and verifiers, fine-tuning policies via rejection sampling, and inference-time scaling.
